_headline: A 1961-vintage EU survey programme, still funded and monthly, confirmed live with a dated press-release schedule and a documented flash-estimate pattern matching eurostat-hicp's own.
_open_questions: DOMAIN: no clean fit in Research.1.md's Domain union -- the ESI/EEI/consumer-confidence indicators are closest to 'monetary-policy' (they feed EU/ECB economic monitoring, per SEC03's own remarks: 'economic monitoring and analysis of economic policies... economic developments in the euro area') but could equally be read as their own unlisted 'business-cycle' or 'sentiment' domain. 'monetary-policy' used as least-wrong, flagged for reconsideration.

Whether an edge exists to esa-2010 or eurostat-hicp was not established -- the budget document's own remarks describe the programme's PURPOSE (monitoring EMU, fiscal surveillance, economic developments) without stating that it USES either as an input. Not stretched into an edge on that basis.

reports.title: Joint Harmonised EU Programme of Business and Consumer Surveys
reports.description: Harmonised monthly surveys of manufacturing, services, retail trade, construction and consumers across EU Member States and candidate countries, producing the Economic Sentiment Indicator (ESI), Employment Expectations Indicator (EEI) and sectoral confidence indicators. SEC03's own remarks (Item 06 20 04 01): 'This appropriation is intended to cover the cost of carrying out the Joint Harmonised EU Programme of Business and Consumer Surveys in the Member States and candidate countries. The programme was initiated by a Commission Decision in November 1961... last approved by Commission Decision C(97) 2241 of 15 July 1997.' DG ECFIN's own landing page: 'an indispensable tool for monitoring the evolution of the EU and the euro area economies.'
reports.cadence_note: Confirmed live via DG ECFIN's own release schedule: 'Latest update: Press release business and consumer survey results (incl. ESI, EEI, EUI, sectoral CIs) - 30 July 2026', with a dated monthly press-release archive. A faster-cadence 'Flash Consumer Confidence Indicator' is also published within the month (23 July 2026, next due 21 August 2026) -- the same flash-estimate pattern already documented for eurostat-hicp.
